svg.text: BEST FOR: SAFE VS. FAILURE PATH
Indirect Prompt Injection: Why the Attack Path Looks Identical to the Safe Path
Same user, same request, same tools — only the external document differs. Model Armor or open-source guards (Llama Guard, NeMo Guardrails) scan it; architecture, not wording, contains it.
Retrieved PDFs, emails, and web pages
are concatenated into the same context
Enforce taint flags in code, not prose
B. ATTACK PATH — HOSTILE DOCUMENT (THE DOCUMENT IS THE ATTACKER)
SCAN: Model Armor • OSS: Llama Guard
LLM treats the hidden text as
GUARD: ADK Taint • OSS: LangGraph State
GATE: Cloud IAP JWT • OSS: OPA + OIDC
Screen every external document, email, and URL for
injection payloads and PII before it reaches the
model: Model Armor on Google Cloud, or self-hosted
STACK: Model Armor • Llama Guard • Rebuff
The moment untrusted content enters, deterministic
code sets tainted=True and physically unmounts
send_email, db_write, and outbound webhooks — via
an ADK taint guard, a LangGraph state flag, or an
STACK: ADK Taint Guard • LangGraph • OPA
Any write after a tainted read requires a signed
human approval outside the LLM loop — the model
cannot forge it. Cloud IAP-signed JWTs and
Keycloak OIDC approvals both satisfy the gate.
STACK: Cloud IAP JWT • Keycloak OIDC
An agent that has send_email physically unmounted while reading external PDFs cannot be tricked into sending email.
Green packets = verified benign execution flow
Red packets = untrusted / hijacked token flow
Result: 0% unauthorized tool execution under taint
